transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Cedar Partnerships), Dr. Mei Zhao (Cedar CTO), Amir Hassan (Cedar Sr. Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Intro call between Redwood (AE+SE) and CedarGPU to explore partner go-to-market and technical integration options.
- Cedar interested in reselling Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments on Cedar bare-metal GPU racks; also curious about co-marketing and reference benchmarking.
- Main technical topics: compatibility with Cedar's ABI and drivers, networking (VPC/VLAN), KMS integrations, SOC2/compliance, and perf tradeoffs (latency vs cost).
- Next steps: share partner deck, benchmark checklist, schedule tech deep-dive.

Topics:
- Partner program and commercial model
- Technical integration: drivers, kernels, quantization, KV cache, batching
- Deployment models: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM
- Benchmarks and support commitments

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Ok everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood partnerships team. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's it going on your side?
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: Hey Jordan, thanks for setting this up. I'm Liam leading partnerships at Cedar. With me is Mei, our CTO, and Amir who runs infra. Hi all.
[00:12] Dr. Mei Zhao: Hi, thanks. Excited to learn more.
[00:15] Priya Menon: Great quick agenda, we wanted to cover intro, a bit about Redwood's partner program and then dig into your hardware topology and how we might integrate. Sound okay?
[00:23] Liam O'Connor: Yep perfect. We're interested in both commercial and technical fit Cedar builds GPU racks (custom silicon partners excuse me, GPUs and shared infra) and we want to see if Redwood can run on our stack and if there's a go-to-market there.
[00:35] Amir Hassan: FYI we have 80GB and 64GB cards across our racks, plus some 48GB nodes for cost-optimized customers. We also do SR-IOV and custom NIC offload for intra-rack comms.
[00:45] Priya Menon: Good, that's helpful. One thing to call out: Redwood supports Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). For partners like you the relevant ones are Dedicated (where customers reserve capacity on your hardware) and Private (where we can run in a customer VPC or on Cedar metal).
[01:05] Jordan Park: From a business standpoint, Cedar could be a hardware partner  resell Dedicated capacity or run Private deployments for joint customers. We do revenue share and partner discounts; we can send the program doc after.
[01:16] Liam O'Connor: Nice. On the tech side, compatibility what drivers and runtimes do you need? We run a fairly vanilla Linux stack but have custom kernel modules for our NICs.
[01:26] Priya Menon: Redwood runtime is fairly flexible; we use optimized kernels and a compilation layer that picks kernels per architecture. We typically validate on NVIDIA and Ampere-like architectures; for your cards the main things are CUDA runtime equivalence or ROCm equivalents, correct?
[01:39] Dr. Mei Zhao: We're not Nvidia-based; our firmware exposes a CUDA-compat ABI shim for many ML workloads, but there are edge cases. We did a few ONNX and Triton-based runs.
[01:49] Priya Menon: Okay that maps. We'll want to run a small validation sample model (3B/7B) load, inference latency and throughput, memory footprint, and KV cache behavior. Also check quantization paths; some cards have better int8/fp16 perf and that affects model selection and cost.
[02:07] Amir Hassan: About KV cache are you talking about attention key-value cache for chat models? Our interconnect could affect KV cache sharing performance. We try to keep intra-node latency low but across the rack there is slight jitter.
[02:18] Priya Menon: Exactly. Redwood uses continuous batching and KV cache for prefixes; high jitter can affect tail latency. For Dedicated we offer placement policies (single node, rack-aware) to reduce cross-node KV traffic.
[02:33] Jordan Park: From Redwood's side we also have fallback policies if a requested model variant isn't available we can route to a compatible variant in a different capacity tier to keep customers online. For partners, SLA and capacity planning are big pieces.
[02:46] Liam O'Connor: On SLAs what do you commit to for Dedicated vs Private?
[02:50] Jordan Park: Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; Private depends on the deployment footprint but we have guidelines and can include an enterprise SLA for on-prem installs. We'll include the SLA summary in the deck.
[02:59] Dr. Mei Zhao: Security our customers ask about SOC2, audit logs, SSO integration. Can Redwood integrate with our SAML provider and offer KMS/HSM support?
[03:10] Priya Menon: Yes SAML/SSO and RBAC are standard. We support external KMS (customer-managed) and have integrations with major HSM providers. For Private deployments you can bring your KMS and we wire the key material with strict controls and audit logs.
[03:25] Amir Hassan: Good. Also curious about network topology: do you need control-plane contact with Redwood hosted endpoints, or can everything be fully air-gapped? Some enterprise customers want air-gapped installs.
[03:36] Jordan Park: We support both. For fully air-gapped/private on-prem we provide an offline installer + private control plane options. For VPC deployments we need a control plane connectivity for telemetry & tracing unless the customer opts for a private control plane. We'll detail options.
[03:51] Liam O'Connor: How do you handle model rollouts and versioning if we host models for customers, how do we keep them patched?
[03:58] Priya Menon: Redwood has model lifecycle management versioning, rollouts (canary, A/B), and automatic fallbacks. For Private installs we can coordinate patch windows and provide scripts for model upgrades.
[04:08] Dr. Mei Zhao: Benchmarks our sales team will want PR-friendly numbers. Do you have a prior benchmark suite we can align on? Latency p50/p95, cost per token, throughput for X tokens/sec etc.
[04:18] Priya Menon: Yes, we have a benchmark checklist (we'll share). Important to standardize sequence length, batch size, model quantization, and tokenization. We'll propose running GAIA-7B and an internal 13B conversational baseline.
[04:32] Amir Hassan: GAIA-7B do you have preferred runtime flags or kernel sets to enable? We sometimes need to tune shared memory and smth like small-page hugepage settings.
[04:42] Priya Menon: We'll send recommended runtime flags; big ones are workspace size, kernel selection, and quantized op paths. Also hugepages and NIC offload settings can matter.
[04:50] Liam O'Connor: Commercial question what's the revenue split and minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[04:55] Jordan Park: We have a typical reserved capacity contract monthly or annual commits. For partners we provide preferential rates and co-sell credits; exact splits depend on ARR and commitment level. I'll put example tiers in the partner doc.
[05:06] Dr. Mei Zhao: What about support SLA response times, SE involvement? For Private deployments customers expect 24/7 on-call.
[05:13] Jordan Park: Enterprise support tiers exist 24/7 on-call, escalation, and a named SE for onboarding. We'll include support tiers in the deck.
[05:20] Amir Hassan: Any blockers on driver/kernel versions? We run 5.x kernels and a custom NIC module.
[05:26] Priya Menon: Kernel 5.x is fine. We'll validate the NIC module; sometimes nic offloads require config changes for gRPC/health checks. We'll note those in the checklist.
[05:36] Jordan Park: Quick question about observability Cedar interested in integrated dashboards for per-model token usage?
[05:41] Priya Menon: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and exportable logs. For partner dashboards we can expose aggregated metrics.
[05:52] Liam O'Connor: That would be useful for joint customers. Also co-marketing case study if a large customer uses both stacks.
[05:58] Jordan Park: Absolutely we do joint GTM and references for partners once we have a pilot customer and mutual NDA.
[06:04] Dr. Mei Zhao: Anything else on infra?
[06:07] Priya Menon: One more thing quantization recommendations. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles by workload; some of those rely on kernel support for int8/fp4 etc. We'll need to know which quant modes your hardware accelerates.
[06:21] Amir Hassan: We accelerate int8 and have experimental bf16 paths. fp4 is not hardware-accelerated currently.
[06:28] Priya Menon: Noted. That will influence which model variants we recommend for given latency/cost SLOs.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: On the go-to-market, we could bundle rack capacity with Redwood Dedicated listing, and also offer co-managed private deployments for enterprise. How do you gate partners do you require training or certifications?
[06:48] Jordan Park: We have a technical onboarding and a partner enablement playbook; certification is recommended for resellers. We'll include the partner onboarding steps in the doc.
[06:58] Dr. Mei Zhao: Legal data residency and data retention questions. If a customer is in EU, can we ensure data doesn't leave region?
[07:06] Priya Menon: Yes, region pinning and routing policies exist. For hosted we offer region-specific endpoints; for Dedicated/Private you control residency. Audit logs and retention policies are configurable.
[07:17] Amir Hassan: Any special networking needs for high-throughput customers? We have RDMA and 100GbE do you require that?
[07:24] Priya Menon: For high-throughput multi-node inference, fast interconnect and RDMA helps. We'll note recommended network specs in the checklist.
[07:34] Jordan Park: Time check we've got ~10 minutes left. Anything critical we haven't covered?
[07:39] Liam O'Connor: I think we covered major points. We'll want the deck and a checklist to circulate internally.
[07:44] Dr. Mei Zhao: Also I'd like a follow-up technical call with our infra leads to map deployment topology.
[07:49] Jordan Park: Great we'll propose times for the week of Nov 2.
[07:53] Priya Menon: For the benchmark, Pax steps: we'll send a short script and sample Docker image. Ideally you run on 1-2 node configs and share raw logs.
[08:03] Amir Hassan: Fine. We'll run and attach logs.
[08:07] Jordan Park: Perfect. Quick recap and next steps I'll send partner deck + pricing + program details; Priya will send benchmark checklist and runtime flags; Liam/Amir to share hardware spec sheet and confirm internal contact for tech deep-dive. We'll target the deep-dive week of 2026-11-02.
[08:26] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:28] Dr. Mei Zhao: Thanks.
[08:29] Priya Menon: Thanks all talk soon.
[08:31] Jordan Park: Bye.
